subject: Assessing connection strategy for EdgeWorks private deployment
messages:
From: Alex Delgado <alex.delgado@edgeworks.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: EdgeWorks Security <security@edgeworks.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Connection strategy question for private deployment

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We wanted to capture our constraints and get your recommendation on the best connectivity pattern for our upcoming private deployment: VPC peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), or a site-to-site VPN to our on-prem datacenter. High-level constraints: 

- PCI and HIPAA scope: must not transit public internet for app->model traffic.
- Our org requires explicit endpoint control and narrow ACLs.
- Multi-region: primary in us-west-2, DR in us-east-1.
- Some legacy on-prem services will need occasional access to the inference endpoints.
- We expect sustained 2–3 Gbps during peak inference traffic, bursts higher.

Can you sketch the tradeoffs and call out any blockers (IP overlap, bandwidth, cross-region costs, monitoring gaps)? We've attached a short requirements doc.

Would prefer a short 30m call this week to align on a recommended approach.

Cheers,
Alex
Principal Infra Eng, EdgeWorks

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Alex Delgado <alex.delgado@edgeworks.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connection strategy question for private deployment

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the requirements doc. Quick summary up-front: for a production-grade private deployment with your compliance requirements and endpoint control needs, we generally recommend a PrivateLink-first approach for customer-facing inference endpoints, combined with selective VPC peering for internal cross-account services and a dedicated Site-to-Site VPN only for legacy on-prem integrations or administrative access.

Key tradeoffs (high level):
- PrivateLink (recommended for prod):
  - Pros: strong isolation (consumer creates ENIs to Redwoods' NLB/endpoint), fine-grained security groups, no IP overlap required on customer side, traffic stays within the cloud provider network without transiting public internet, good for PCI/HIPAA.
  - Cons: per-connection endpoint costs and some additional management for multi-region fallback (need endpoint per region).

- VPC Peering (good for lower-latency intra-VPC workloads):
  - Pros: low-latency, no additional endpoints to manage, cheaper for high bandwidth intra-region traffic.
  - Cons: not transitive across peered VPCs (complex mesh if you have many VPCs), IP CIDR planning required (no overlap), cross-region peering has inter-region data charges.

- Site-to-site VPN (legacy/overflow path):
  - Pros: straightforward to stand up for on-prem, encrypted over internet or AWS-managed tunnels, useful for admin/maintenance paths.
  - Cons: not great for sustained multi-gigabit traffic (unless you use multiple tunnels/HA appliances or Direct Connect/Carrier), potential latency and jitter, counts as public transit unless you front with PrivateLink + VPN for admin traffic.

Immediate blockers to check:
1) CIDR overlap between EdgeWorks VPCs and Redwood's endpoints/peers. If overlap exists, PrivateLink avoids the problem.
2) Bandwidth profile: sustained multi-Gbps favors peering or dedicated interconnect/Direct Connect rather than standard VPN.
3) DR failover model: PrivateLink requires endpoint presence in DR region and route management for failover.

Next steps I propose:
- Quick 30m design sync to confirm CIDRs and traffic numbers (I can bring Karthik).
- We'll produce a 1-page recommendation + diagram and a cost sketch (endpoint vs peering egress) by end of week.

Attached a short matrix (internal) that maps common patterns to recommended usage.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Looping in a few implementation notes from infra: 

- IP overlap: if EdgeWorks has 10.0.0.0/8 usage internally we recommend reserving a dedicated /16 for the VPCs that will talk to Redwood; peering requires non-overlapping ranges across accounts. PrivateLink avoids this entirely since it uses ENIs in the consumer VPC.

- Bandwidth/cost: at 2–3 Gbps sustained, peering + inter-region peering is cheaper for egress compared to many PrivateLink connections (PrivateLink has per-GB + per-hour costs on the endpoint). If you need guaranteed throughput, consider AWS Direct Connect or cloud provider's dedicated interconnect (we can model Direct Connect + PrivateLink combo).

- Cross-region: peering between us-west-2 and us-east-1 is supported but has inter-region data transfer charges. PrivateLink requires endpoints in each region; failover becomes a matter of DNS/route steering.

- Monitoring and tracing: with PrivateLink you still get request-level tracing from Redwood (we inject trace headers), but underlying network metrics (ENI throughput) live in your account — we'll provide dashboards and cross-account monitor role. For peering, you'll need VPC flow logs aggregated across accounts to get the same visibility.

- Security posture: PrivateLink gives a single network entry point; combined with security groups and AWS NACLs it's easier to satisfy scoped audits. Peering expands the network surface unless you restrict routes carefully.

Happy to cover these in the call — can demo a small PrivateLink proof-of-concept if that helps.

-Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex — following up with a concise recommendation and next steps after reviewing requirements and Karthik's notes.

Recommendation (short):
- Prod inference endpoints: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) in each region where you run inference. Rationale: strict network boundary, audit-friendly, avoids CIDR overlap issues, and keeps traffic off the public internet to meet PCI/HIPAA needs.
- Internal, high-throughput intra-account services (batch preprocessing, model orchestration): use VPC peering where latency and sustained throughput matter, but keep peering limited to known accounts and CIDR-safe ranges.
- On-prem legacy systems: use an HA Site-to-Site VPN for admin/maintenance and occasional traffic; for heavy production traffic from on-prem, prefer Direct Connect or equivalent carrier interconnect into the VPC + PrivateLink.

Operational notes / next steps:
1) Please confirm your VPC CIDRs for the VPC(s) that will host inference clients and any existing peered VPCs. If you have overlapping ranges, we'll default to PrivateLink.
2) We'll produce a final architecture diagram (attached) and a short cost delta table (PrivateLink endpoints across two regions vs peering egress + Direct Connect).
3) Schedule: 30m design review this Friday 11:00–11:30 PT? I'll invite Marcus for monitoring and Karthik for infra specifics.

Attachments: redwood-arch-diagram-v1.png (png) — high-level layout showing PrivateLink per region + peering for internal services.

If that aligns, I'll produce a one-page decision memo to include in your compliance package.

Best,
Priyom
